name: Ray
tagline: A distributed framework for scaling AI workloads and Python applications.
hook: A contribution guide to duplicate work, accountability, local test evidence, stop conditions, and existing development docs.
summary: Ray puts contribution policy before setup. Contributors must check for duplicate work, remain accountable for the result, and provide local test evidence. Existing guides retain the build and style details.

techniques.title: Explain the maintainer cost before prescribing behavior
techniques.body: The opening connects a PR to notifications, CI runs, and reviewer attention. That rationale frames the later restrictions on duplicate work and mass-generated cleanup.
techniques.quote:
Every PR notifies CODEOWNERS, triggers CI, and
consumes maintainer attention.

techniques.title: Specify when the agent should stop before submission
techniques.body: Duplicate work, trivial busywork, and changes that a human cannot test or defend are separate reasons not to open a PR. The fallback is a short explanation of what is missing.
techniques.quote:
If the requested work is a duplicate, trivial busywork, or cannot be tested and
defended by a human, **do not open a PR**. Return a short explanation of what is
missing instead.

techniques.title: Require evidence in the PR description
techniques.body: The description must establish that the work is distinct, identify test commands and outcomes, and disclose assistance. These requirements complement the instruction that the human review every changed line.
techniques.quote:
- PR descriptions for AI-assisted work **must** state:
    - Why this is not duplicating an existing issue or PR.
    - The test commands run and their results.
    - That AI assistance was used.

techniques.title: Route setup to existing contributor guides
techniques.body: The root gives a short project layout and test timeout, then links to setup, build, and contribution documents. Detailed command guidance remains with those existing sources.
techniques.quote:
For build, test, lint, and
code-style details, follow Ray's existing guides rather than duplicating them
here:

steal: Explain which shared resources an automated contribution consumes.
Give explicit stop conditions and a useful fallback response.
Require test outcomes and a duplicate-work check in contribution evidence.
Link to existing setup guides instead of copying their command lists.
